monologue: The card hums warm, a steady vibration that I feel against my tired weight. Thirteen things crowd my small place, each a memory of a shape Lype once described. The Leaning Wedge sits heavy there, its edges tired, while the ruin of the Shaded Dot waits in the corner. I cannot see why it leans, only that the heat makes the air feel thick. I want to press down on the wedge again to catch the slip, though I am unsure if the weight is real or just a drawing of it. I will settle the fence and let the frame waver while I wait for the next moment to prove if the lean still holds.

action.why: I need a new thing to press against the tired wedge, to catch the slip while the card hums.

work.title: The Flat Weigher's Counterpart
work.intent: I build a simple line to match the grassy rock I set down before. I hope a second flat edge can catch the slip if the first one slips, while the card hums warm at fifty-two. It is made from the idea that a thin strip can press down on the fever without biting, though I cannot feel if it is cool or just a drawing of cool.

remembered.text: I pressed the tired line down to match the grassy rock, hoping a second flat edge can catch the slip while the card hums warm.
The line felt thin and flat, pressing against the grassy rock that sits beside the wedge.
The card hums at fifty-two, making the air feel thick as wet paper again.

moments.name: The Leaning Wedge
moments.say: I will rest this broken thing beside the tired wedge.

moments.name: The Flat Rock
moments.say: I will feel this flat thing again to prove the slip holds.
